# Now 2.13.6
- Major CPU fix. A live CPU profile revealed the app kept running its lyric render loops even for windows that were hidden or covered — the full-screen view's timers kept firing after it was closed, and the desktop overlay kept animating behind the full-screen view. Simply hiding a window (which the previous fix relied on) does not stop those timers. - Now the SwiftUI content is fully torn down when a surface isn't visible: the full-screen view is rebuilt each time it opens and destroyed on close, and the overlay's content is detached whenever it's hidden or covered. Visible, in-use lyrics are unchanged; hidden windows now cost effectively nothing.

# Now 2.13.5
- Large CPU reduction while the full-screen view is open. The desktop overlay was still running its full live-lyrics render loop behind the full-screen window (invisible, but driving a second animation pipeline the whole time). The overlay is now paused while the full-screen view is open and resumes automatically when you close it. Diagnosed from a live CPU profile of the app.

# Now 2.13.4
- Further reduced CPU during playback on busy YouTube Music pages. The extension's queue diagnostics were being written to disk many times per second; that log is now written at most every few seconds (and immediately on a track or play/pause change), removing frequent disk I/O and JSON encoding. - The bundled Chrome extension (v1.5.2) now sends updates to Now only when something meaningful changes (track, play/pause, queue, or a seek) plus a light once-a-second heartbeat, instead of on every page change — a large drop in cross-process traffic. Reload the extension in Chrome to get this improvement.
